subject: Credibility intervals for linear predictor conditional on random effects

messages.author: b548117c8aed3bfb
messages.subject: Credibility intervals for linear predictor conditional on random effects
parts:
Hi,
Is there a way to simulate predictions with inla that are conditional on the mean random effect in a random effects model?
For instance, I have a model like this:
inla(y ~ x +
            f(grp, model = "iid"),
    data = dmod, family = "gaussian",
    control.predictor = list(link = 1))

Where x is a continuous covaraite and grp is a factor giving group levels. I want to get the 95% CIs for values of y across the range of x values, conditional on the mean value of 'grp' (ie = 0). 
e.g. if using frequentist inference, you can do this with the lme4 package by boostrapping over the covariate but not the random effects (ie bootMer this is the option use.u = TRUE).

A reproducible example is given here:  https://github.com/cbrown5/uncertainty-intervals/blob/master/inla-marginal-conditional-intervals.R
Also see figures here: https://github.com/cbrown5/uncertainty-intervals

I know INLA derives its convenience by estimating only the marginals, but I had though that inla.posterior.sample() might be the solution, however it seems the quantiles of the posterior samples are also marginals.

Thanks,
Chris

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Credibility intervals for linear predictor conditional on random effects
parts:
Hi,

inla.posterior.sample() samples E(y|the rest), not y|rest. You have to add the error term. See the GAG urine example in http://www.leg.ufpr.br/~elias/cursos/br2015/rinla.pdf

Elias
